question.value: Is cold molecular gas falling onto the SMBH of the young radio AGN PKS B1718-649, and does it fuel the radio source (e.g. via chaotic cold accretion)?

evidence.quote: If this was the case, higher resolution and sensitivity observations of the molecular gas in the central regions of the galaxy could provide us a detailed view of the interplay between the gas and the nuclear activity

findings_qualitative.value: CO emission traces a clumpy warped disk, with an edge-on east-west circumnuclear disk of radius 700 pc

evidence.quote: The rotating structure is oriented along the east-west direction (PA $=72^\circ$), it has a radius of $700$ pc.

claims.hypothesis: Cold molecular clouds fall onto the SMBH of the young radio AGN
claims.experiment: CO(2-1) absorption against the compact 230 GHz continuum compared with red-shifted H2
claims.result: Absorption at +365 km/s offset, co-spatial with red-shifted H2 within 75 pc
claims.finding: Molecular clouds are likely falling onto the SMBH, consistent with chaotic cold accretion

evidence.quote: Likely, these clouds are accreting onto the SMBH.

claims.hypothesis: The molecular gas is distributed in a warped disk
claims.result: Kinematic major axis changes from north-south to east-west
claims.finding: Warped disk with 700 pc circumnuclear disk

evidence.quote: Likely, also the molecular gas of PKS B1718–649 is distributed in a similar warped disk.

claims.hypothesis: Central gas conditions differ from the outer disk
claims.experiment: Compare H2 column density from H2 1-0 S(1) and CO(2-1)
claims.result: Ratio 110 within 75 pc vs 16 in the disk
claims.finding: CO may be photo-dissociated near the AGN

evidence.quote: is ten times higher than in the circumnuclear disk

why_this_method.value: Young compact radio source chosen because jets have not yet perturbed the ISM

evidence.quote: The ideal candidate would be a very young radio source, where the radio jets extend for at most a few parsecs

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Bar-induced non-circular motions mimicking a warp ruled out: no bar signature in residuals

evidence.quote: The residuals (Fig. [4](#fig:stars)) show that no signature of a bar is found.

limitations_admitted.value: Only CO(2-1) available; cannot constrain temperature, pressure, heating

evidence.quote: do not allow us to constrain the physical conditions of the circumnuclear disk, such as temperature, pressure and heating mechanism of the gas

referee_caveats_inferred: Excitation temperature of 16 K assumed; column densities are lower limits
Infall inferred from velocity sign and line of sight; distance relies on H2 coincidence at low resolution
Accretion rate range spans three orders of magnitude
Continuum variable and half of cm extrapolation
